title: Configuration you can explain in every environment
outcome: Bind and validate configuration, separate secrets, and diagnose which setting actually won.
useCase: The same service deployed to several environments.
benefits: Clear startup failures and reproducible runtime behavior.
drawbacks: Configuration precedence and secret delivery still need operational ownership.
cue: Bind it. Validate it. Know where it came from.

trace.title: Property sources
trace.detail: Configuration changes behavior without changing the application’s source. That makes it powerful and easy to misunderstand. A value may come from a file, profile, environment variable, command line, or remote source. Record the effective value and its source without logging secrets.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Boot prepares environment properties → binds a settings object → validates it → creates dependent clients → starts serving traffic. A bad required setting should fail at a clear boundary.

In a test, supply an invalid max-attempts and verify startup rejects it. Then verify the intended profile chooses the fake integration. A unit test constructing the settings object does not prove binding/validation wiring.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: A default secret committed to a property file is still a secret. A profile name such as prod does not prove that the right database or network was selected.
